title: Astrid and the Well
premise: Wendell Ishikawa takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Hollow Creek, where students vanish one by one and the town's oldest families keep signing a strange lease on a house called the Well. When her childhood imaginary friend Astrid appears on her porch—real, unchanged, and terrified—Wendell is dragged into the truth: the town survives by feeding the Well a child every generation, and this year the last resident, dying matriarch Cora Vane, must sign the papers that renew the covenant. Wendell, who lost her own sister to a similar bargain decades ago, must choose between exposing the town and saving the child already marked. In the end she burns the papers at sunrise, breaking the covenant—but the Well takes a substitute: Astrid, who was never imaginary at all but the sister Wendell forgot she had.
about_author: Dominic Reyes is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in small mountain towns before turning to horror full-time. His work draws on Appalachian folklore and the quiet cruelties of communities that keep their bargains.

chapters.title: The Long Road Down
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Wendell's POV as she arrives in Hollow Creek, passing a shuttered school wing and a wellhead fenced with iron. She notes the town's too-polite welcome. Emotional beat: wary optimism masking old grief over her sister's disappearance.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: Wendell's first week teaching; twenty-two students become twenty-one after a boy named Eli stops attending. The principal deflects smoothly. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the first crack of unease beneath professional routine.

chapters.title: Astrid on the Porch
chapters.summary: At dusk, Wendell finds Astrid—her childhood imaginary friend, ageless, unchanged—waiting on her porch steps. Astrid warns her not to sign anything and vanishes when named aloud. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past asserting itself as present danger.

chapters.title: The Vane House
chapters.summary: Wendell visits Cora Vane, the town's last original resident, to ask about Eli. Cora is lucid, cruel, and counting days on a wall calendar. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: dread dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: A student, Marisol, draws the Well in class and whispers that 'the thirsty year' is coming. Other children go silent around her. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: protective anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Records
chapters.summary: In the school basement Wendell finds enrollment ledgers going back 140 years—every missing child listed under 'transferred,' always in years ending in the same digit. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the pattern is real.

chapters.title: Astrid Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid appears again and begins telling Wendell things only her dead sister could know—the lullaby, the scar, the promise made at the wellhead. POV: alternating Wendell/Astrid. Emotional beat: hope curdling toward an unbearable hypothesis.

chapters.title: The Lease
chapters.summary: Wendell discovers the town charter: Hollow Creek holds its land via a perpetual lease renewed each generation by the last resident's signature—and a payment. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the horror becomes bureaucratic, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Eli Comes Back
chapters.summary: Eli returns to school hollow-eyed, unable to say where he was, scratching well-water stains into his desk. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: pity and terror; he is a returned warning.

chapters.title: Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Wendell confronts the town council publicly; they respond not with denial but with pity, explaining what the Well buys them—no famine, no fire, no flood since 1889. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: isolation; justice has no audience here.

chapters.title: Marisol's Name
chapters.summary: Wendell realizes the ledger pattern points to Marisol as this generation's payment. Astrid confirms it and begs Wendell to leave before sunrise of the signing. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: love against duty—her duty to the child versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Cora's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying Cora tells Wendell about the night in 1974 when Wendell's own family signed away her sister, and how Astrid is what remained. POV: Cora, then Wendell. Emotional beat: grief detonating; the truth about what was invited in.

chapters.title: They Come for Consent
chapters.summary: Councilmen visit Wendell's house at night, politely asking her to stop digging, leaving a blank signature page 'in case she'd like to help.' POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: menace wearing civility's face.

chapters.title: Hiding Marisol
chapters.summary: Wendell hides Marisol in her home as the town searches; neighbors' porch lights sweep the streets like searchlights. Astrid stands guard. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: siege intimacy; found family under threat.

chapters.title: The Well Speaks
chapters.summary: Through Eli, the Well speaks in the classroom's silence, offering Wendell her sister back if she delivers Marisol. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fence
chapters.summary: Marisol, guilt-ridden, slips out to give herself up; Wendell and Astrid race through the fog to the wellhead. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: panic and fierce love.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: At the Vane house, Cora lifts the pen as the town gathers; Wendell bursts in and demands the papers, reading the covenant's true terms aloud—the Well keeps what it's given, forever, including Astrid. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: climax of truth against complicity.

chapters.title: Fire at Sunrise
chapters.summary: Wendell sets the lease alight as dawn breaks; the town screams, the ground shudders, and the Well, unbound, reaches for a substitute. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: defiant sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Well Took
chapters.summary: The ground stills. Astrid is gone—pulled down in Wendell's place, the sister-shaped debt finally paid. Wendell kneels at the iron fence holding Astrid's ribbon. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: devastating cost of survival.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Weeks later: no more disappearances, the town hollowed by shame, Marisol safe in Wendell's care. Eli wakes and remembers nothing. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: exhausted, guilty peace.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Cora dies unsigned, freeing the land; the town must now survive on its own merits or fail honestly. Wendell decides to stay and teach. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, chosen daily.

chapters.title: Astrid and the Well
chapters.summary: On the final morning, Wendell hears the lullaby rising faintly from the wellhead—not menacing, but waiting. She answers it by name. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: mourning braided with love; some doors never fully close.
